items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive.

items.title: Augmented vs. Artificial Intelligence in Medicine — CASRAI
items.summary: Researchers, clinical informaticists, and health system governance committees searching for augmented intelligence vs artificial intelligence need a precise regulatory and operational distinction between assistive human-in-the-loop tools and autonomous algorithmic systems. While computer science uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an umbrella term for machine learning and statistical inference models, the American Medical Association (AMA) codified Augmented Intelligence in House of Delegates [...] Autonomous Artificial Intelligence (Human-out-of-the-Loop): The computational system processes raw clinical inputs (such as retinal fundus photographs or continuous waveform telemetry) and outputs a definitive diagnostic classification or workflow directive without requiring a qualified specialist to independently interpret the underlying signal. [...] Augmented Intelligence (Assistive / Human-in-the-Loop): The computational system aggregates longitudinal EHR records, highlights relevant clinical guidelines, or drafts documentation, but presents both the recommendation and its verifiable evidentiary basis to a licensed clinician. The clinician independently evaluates the rationale, integrates physical exam findings and patient preferences, and retains unrestricted authority to accept, modify, or override the output.

items.title: New FAA artificial-intelligence software is helping cut flight delays at DFW Airport, federal officials say
items.summary: A new artificial intelligence-powered air traffic control software is being used to reduce commercial flight delays at DFW International Airport, a groundbreaking development for North Texas’ airspace operations, according to the U.S. Department of Transportation. [...] The use of SMART was first deployed in September to assist Washington, D.C.-area airports. The software has since been expanded to air route traffic control centers in Jacksonville, Fla.; Miami; and Atlanta. The tool has since helped reroute nearly 180 flights across the U.S., improving flight times by more than 10 minutes and saving nearly 80 gallons of fuel on average, the department said. [...] “We’re rolling out new tools like SMART in Dallas-Fort Worth that uses super intelligence to help our incredible air traffic controllers save Texans valuable flight time,” U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement. “SMART will slash frustrating delays, reduce stress on air traffic controllers, and lower travel prices.”

items.title: Công nghệ gen tạo động lực đột phá cho ngành nông nghiệp
items.summary:
Giai đoạn 2026-2030, Việt Nam đặt mục tiêu xy dựng ít nhất 5 phòng thí nghiệm trọng điểm và 5 phòng thí nghiệm chuyên ngành hiện đại, tập trung vào công nghệ gen, công nghệ tế bào thực vật và động vật, vi sinh vật, thú y và chẩn đoán dịch bệnh. Mục tiêu đến năm 2035, tầm nhìn đến năm 2045 là làm chủ hoàn toàn công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới và công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen để tạo ra các sản phẩm thương mại phục vụ thị trường trong nước và xuất khẩu. [...] Được xếp vào danh mục công nghệ chiến lược cấp quốc gia, công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen, đặc biệt là CRISPR/Cas, đang mở ra vận hội lớn để nông nghiệp Việt Nam chủ động thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu và bảo đảm an ninh lương thực.

Các chuyên gia quốc tế khẳng định, kỹ thuật chỉnh sửa gen, tiêu biểu là CRISPR/Cas, mang lại bước tiến mang tính cách mạng nhờ khả năng can thiệp chính xác, có chủ đích vào hệ gen mục tiêu mà không đưa vật liệu di truyền ngoại lai vào cơ thể sinh vật. [...] Trong định hướng phát triển khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo phục vụ tái cơ cấu ngành nông nghiệp, công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới ngày càng khẳng định vị trí động lực then chốt. Theo Quyết định số 1131/QĐ-TTg của Thủ tướng Chính phủ về Danh mục công nghệ chiến lược và sản phẩm công nghệ chiến lược, công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen thuộc nhóm công nghệ y - sinh học tiên tiến, được định hướng ưu tiên ứng dụng mạnh mẽ trong y tế và nông nghiệp. Những sáng kiến có khả năng nng cao chất lượng sản phẩm, hiệu quả quản lý và năng suất lao động được khuyến khích tham gia.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. [...] Create opportunities for local workers and businesses.We’ll publish the jobs we expect to create, work with unions and training providers to help residents prepare for them, and report annually on hiring and apprenticeships. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
